2_Introduction: The champion device offers a high PCE of 19.853% for the reverse scan (JSC of 25.644 mA/cm², VOC of 1.1155 V, and FF of 69.4006%). The perovskite ink, prepared from Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.73 mol/L, formed the base layer for subsequent fabrication steps. The perovskite solution was spin-coated on the substrates at 1000 rpm for 10 s and at 5000 rpm for 40 s, respectively. During the spin-coating process, 160 µL of CB antisolvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 10 s before the end of the process. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ at 1.73 mol/L, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—where the small ionic radius of Cs⁺ enhances phase stability and suppresses halide segregation, MA⁺ promotes rapid nucleation but introduces thermal instability, and the dominant FA⁺ stabilizes the black α-phase while optimizing the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) to minimize lattice strain and inhibit unwanted δ-phase formation—thereby yielding a near-ideal bandgap (~1.53 eV) with suppressed ion migration pathways; crystallization is precisely orchestrated by the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for uniform wetting followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for controlled solvent evaporation), where the timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene delivered 10 s before spin cessation triggers instantaneous supersaturation, arresting Ostwald ripening and promoting homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, while the subsequent 110 °C/25 min thermal annealing drives complete solvent removal, facilitates PbI₂-to-perovskite conversion, relieves residual compressive stress (as corroborated by XRD peak narrowing and absence of parasitic PbI₂ reflections at ~12.6°), and enables grain boundary coalescence—collectively yielding large, oriented grains with low trap density, high phase purity, and minimal interfacial voids, as evidenced by uniform film coverage and high grayscale intensity in optical microscopy and PL mapping, which directly suppress non-radiative recombination centers and ensure continuous charge transport pathways; the resulting morphological homogeneity, structural integrity, and defect-minimized bulk translate into prolonged carrier lifetimes (evidenced by intense, uniformly distributed photoluminescence and monoexponential decay kinetics), reduced energetic disorder, and efficient extraction at both electrodes—culminating in a VOC of 1.1155 V, JSC of 25.644 mA/cm², FF of 69.4006%, and PCE of 19.853%.
